city.Guinea-Bissau.description: Guinea-Bissau is a small West African country with dozens of palm-covered islands called the Bijagós. It's famous for cashew nut farms, colorful carnival masks, and warm coastal waters full of fish.

city.Lesotho.description: Lesotho is a tiny mountain kingdom completely surrounded by South Africa. Nicknamed the 'Kingdom in the Sky,' it has snowy peaks, one of Africa's rare ski slopes, and shepherds who ride hardy ponies wrapped in warm blankets.

city.Liberia.description: Liberia sits on the coast of West Africa and was founded in the 1800s as a home for freed American slaves. Its capital, Monrovia, is named after a US president, and its rainforests shelter rare pygmy hippos.
city.Liberia.landmark: river winding through the lush green Sapo rainforest
city.Liberia.greeting: English is the official language — a friendly Liberian hello is “How di body?”

city.Libya.description: Libya is a mostly desert country in North Africa, stretching along the Mediterranean Sea. Almost the whole nation is covered by the Sahara — which even hides a black volcano crater ringed by tiny, brightly colored lakes — while its coastline holds spectacular ancient Roman ruins.
city.Libya.landmark: grand columns and arches of the ancient Roman ruins of Leptis Magna near the sea

city.Madagascar.description: This giant island off the east coast of Africa is home to lemurs and countless other animals found nowhere else on Earth, along with its famous fat-trunked baobab trees.
city.Madagascar.greeting: The language is Malagasy — a friendly hello is “Salama” (sah-LAH-mah).
